breakfast.name: Ful Medames (Stewed Fava Beans)
ingredients: 400g dried fava beans (soaked overnight) or 2 cans
instructions: Simmer soaked fava beans until very tender and starting to break down — hours for dried, or use canned
Mash roughly — some whole, some broken
Stir in crushed garlic, lemon juice, cumin, salt
Serve in bowls, drizzle olive oil and tahini generously
Top with chopped parsley, a hard-boiled egg
Scoop with warm baladi bread
This is Egypt's breakfast — rich, poor, everyone eats ful every morning
The street cart version with the giant copper pot is the most viral Egyptian food image
breakfast.description: Egypt's national breakfast for over 4,000 years — slow-cooked fava beans mashed with garlic, lemon, cumin, and tahini, scooped up with warm flatbread. The street carts with their massive copper pots are iconic, and the communal morning ful ritual is the most filmed food scene in Cairo.

breakfast.name: Ta'ameya (Egyptian Falafel)
ingredients: 500g dried fava beans (soaked overnight — NOT chickpeas)
instructions: Grind soaked raw fava beans (not cooked!) with all the herbs, onion, garlic, leek
The mixture should be bright green inside — this is the key difference from chickpea falafel
Season with cumin, coriander, salt, add baking powder
Shape into flat patties (not balls — Egyptian style is flat)
Press both sides into sesame seeds
Deep fry at 170°C until dark golden crust, bright green interior — about 4 min
Serve in baladi bread with tahini, pickled vegetables, and tomato
The green interior reveal when you bite in is the viral moment
breakfast.description: Egyptian falafel made with fava beans instead of chickpeas — the inside is vivid green from all the fresh herbs. The flat patty shape, sesame crust, and that green interior reveal are what distinguish ta'ameya from every other falafel and make it endlessly shareable on social media.

breakfast.name: Feteer Meshaltet (Egyptian Layered Pastry)
ingredients: Toppings — sweet: honey, powdered sugar, clotted cream (ishta) / savory: cheese, minced meat, egg
instructions: Make soft dough, rest 30 min
Divide into balls, oil generously
Stretch each ball paper-thin on an oiled surface — you should see through it
Spread with ghee, fold into layers, stretch again, more ghee, fold again
Repeat stretching and folding 4-5 times — building dozens of paper-thin layers
Shape into round, place on hot griddle or in oven at 220°C
Bake until golden and puffed with flaky, shattering layers
Can be sweet (drizzled with honey and cream) or savory (stuffed with cheese)
The flaky layer reveal when torn apart is mesmerizing
breakfast.description: Egypt's most dramatic pastry — dough stretched paper-thin and folded with ghee dozens of times, creating a flaky, shattering, buttery layered pie. The stretching technique and the layer-reveal when you tear it open have made feteer one of the most viral Egyptian food videos. Sweet with honey and cream, or stuffed savory.

lunch.name: Koshari (Egypt's National Dish)
ingredients: Tomato sauce: tomatoes, garlic, vinegar, chili
Da'a sauce: garlic, vinegar, lemon juice, cumin, chili
instructions: Cook rice, lentils, and pasta separately
Make tomato sauce: garlic, tomatoes, vinegar, chili — cook until thick and tangy
Make da'a: crush garlic with vinegar, lemon, cumin, chili
Fry sliced onions until deeply caramelized and crispy
Layer in bowl: rice-lentil mix, then pasta, then chickpeas
Pour tomato sauce over everything
Drizzle da'a for heat and tang
Crown with a mountain of crispy fried onions
Mix everything together before eating — the combination is greater than its parts
This is Cairo's most beloved street food — every neighborhood has a koshari shop
lunch.description: Egypt's beloved carb-on-carb national dish — rice, lentils, pasta, and chickpeas layered with spicy tomato sauce, tangy garlic vinegar, and a mountain of crispy fried onions. It sounds chaotic but tastes perfect. The assembly-line street vendors and the dramatic onion-pile topping are viral video staples.

lunch.name: Molokhia (Jute Leaf Soup)
ingredients: 500g molokhia leaves (fresh or frozen, finely chopped)
Taqlia: 10 cloves garlic (crushed), 2 tbsp ghee, 1 tbsp ground coriander
instructions: Chop molokhia leaves very finely — almost to a paste (or use frozen pre-chopped)
Bring broth to a boil, add molokhia
Stir — it thickens into a viscous, deep green soup
Make taqlia: fry crushed garlic and coriander in ghee until fragrant and golden
Pour the sizzling taqlia into the molokhia — the dramatic sizzle is essential
Stir well — the garlic aroma transforms everything
Serve over rice with cooked chicken or rabbit on the side
Squeeze lemon juice over your bowl
The slimy texture divides people — Egyptians love it, first-timers are suspicious
lunch.description: Egypt's ancient green soup — finely chopped jute leaves cooked into a viscous, garlicky broth. The dramatic moment when the sizzling garlic taqlia hits the green soup is the most satisfying sound in Egyptian cooking. The divisive slimy texture makes it viral content — you either love or fear molokhia.

lunch.name: Hawawshi (Meat-Stuffed Bread)
instructions: Mix minced meat with onion, tomatoes, peppers, parsley, all spices
Split baladi bread open to create a pocket
Stuff generously with the spiced meat mixture — pack it full
Press closed
Bake in very hot oven (230°C) or press on a hot griddle until bread is crispy and meat is cooked through
The bread should be crunchy, the meat juicy inside
Cut into wedges
This is Egypt's answer to the burger — spiced meat sealed in bread and crisped
lunch.description: Egypt's stuffed bread — spiced minced meat packed inside baladi bread and baked until the bread is shatteringly crispy and the meat is juicy. Essentially Egypt's original hot pocket, predating all fast food. Street vendors pressing hawawshi on griddles are a viral Cairo food scene.

dinner.name: Fattah (Celebration Rice and Bread Dish)
ingredients: Bread layer: stale baladi bread, fried crispy in ghee
Rice layer: Egyptian short-grain rice cooked with vermicelli
Meat: 1kg lamb or beef, slow-cooked until tender
Tomato-vinegar sauce: tomato paste, garlic, vinegar, chili
instructions: Slow-cook meat until falling-apart tender, reserve broth
Fry stale bread pieces in ghee until very crispy
Cook rice with toasted vermicelli (sha'reya)
Make sauce: fry garlic, add tomato paste, vinegar, chili, thin with broth
In a deep dish, layer: crispy bread on bottom
Soak bread with hot broth — it softens underneath but stays crispy on top
Layer rice over the bread
Place meat on top
Pour tomato-vinegar sauce over everything
The layers soak together — crispy bread absorbs broth from below, sauce from above
This is Eid and celebration food — every Egyptian family has their fattah tradition
dinner.description: Egypt's celebration dish — layers of crispy bread soaked in broth, topped with vermicelli rice and tender slow-cooked meat, drenched in a tangy tomato-vinegar-garlic sauce. Served at Eid, weddings, and every major milestone. The layering technique and the dramatic 'flip' presentation are viral food content.

dinner.name: Sayadeya (Egyptian Fish with Rice)
ingredients: 1 whole fish (bass, mullet, or bluefish — skin on)
Onion sauce: 4 large onions (sliced thin, caramelized dark brown), cumin, turmeric
instructions: Caramelize sliced onions very dark — this is the base of all flavor, don't rush it
Blend half the caramelized onions into a paste with cumin, turmeric, fish stock
Season fish, fry until golden on both sides
Cook rice in the onion-spice broth — it turns golden brown
Layer rice on platter, place fish on top
Garnish with remaining caramelized onions, toasted nuts, lemon
The rice should be deep gold from the onion broth — not white
This is Alexandria's and Port Said's coastal pride
dinner.description: Egypt's coastal fish-and-rice — the rice cooked in caramelized onion broth turns deep gold, topped with whole fried fish and toasted nuts. Alexandria's signature dish, where the Nile meets the Mediterranean. The golden onion rice technique has gone viral as a flavor hack beyond Egyptian cuisine.

snacks.name: Dukkah with Bread and Oil
instructions: Toast all nuts and seeds separately — each has a different toasting time
Grind coarsely in mortar and pestle — must be chunky, not a paste
Mix with salt and pepper
To eat: dip bread in olive oil, then press into dukkah
The oil makes the dukkah stick to the bread
Store in a jar — every Egyptian household has a jar of dukkah
The recipe varies by family — some add dried mint, dried thyme, or nigella seeds
snacks.description: Egypt's ancient spice-and-nut blend — toasted hazelnuts, sesame, and warm spices ground coarsely. Bread dipped in olive oil then pressed into dukkah is one of the oldest snacks on Earth. The concept went globally viral when Western food media discovered it as the original 'everything seasoning.'

snacks.name: Alexandrian Liver Sandwich
instructions: Cut liver into small cubes — speed is everything
Heat oil smoking hot
Flash-fry liver, peppers, onion, garlic — high heat, fast, 3-4 min max
Season with cumin, coriander, chili, splash of vinegar
Liver must be just cooked — still pink inside, not rubbery
Stuff into baladi bread with tahini and pickled vegetables
The street vendors cook each sandwich individually, to order, at incredible speed
This is Alexandria's and Cairo's most beloved sandwich
snacks.description: Egypt's most popular street sandwich — cubed liver flash-fried with peppers and spices, stuffed into bread with tahini. The street vendors' speed and wok-tossing skills are legendary. Liver sandwich-making videos are some of the most watched Egyptian street food content online.

desserts.name: Basbousa (Semolina Cake in Syrup)
ingredients: Syrup: 2 cups sugar, 1 cup water, lemon juice, rosewater
instructions: Mix semolina, sugar, yogurt, melted butter, baking powder, vanilla, coconut
Pour into greased pan, smooth top
Score into diamond shapes
Place an almond on each diamond
Bake at 180°C for 25-30 min until golden
Meanwhile make syrup: boil sugar and water, add lemon juice, rosewater
Pour COLD syrup over HOT cake — this is the rule, never hot on hot
Let absorb for at least 30 min before serving
The cake should be moist and soaked through, not dry
desserts.description: Egypt's beloved semolina cake soaked in rosewater syrup — scored into diamonds, each topped with an almond. The 'cold syrup on hot cake' rule is sacred (never the reverse). The satisfying diamond-cutting moment and the syrup-soaking technique are viral baking content across the Middle East.

desserts.name: Umm Ali (Egyptian Bread Pudding)
ingredients: Mixed nuts: pistachios, almonds, walnuts, pine nuts
instructions: Break puff pastry into pieces, toast until golden
Layer in baking dish with nuts, raisins, coconut
Heat milk with sugar and vanilla
Pour hot milk over pastry — let it soak
Pour cream over the top
Bake at 200°C until top is golden and bubbling
Serve hot — it's a warm, creamy, nutty pudding
Named 'Mother of Ali' — legend says it was made to celebrate a political victory in the 13th century
desserts.description: Egypt's legendary bread pudding — puff pastry soaked in sweetened milk with nuts, raisins, and coconut, baked until golden and bubbling. Named after a 13th-century queen, it's the ultimate Egyptian comfort dessert. The bubbling-out-of-the-oven moment is pure viral comfort food content.

drinks.name: Karkade (Hibiscus Tea)
instructions: For hot: steep dried hibiscus in boiling water 10 min, strain, sweeten
For cold (more popular in summer): soak hibiscus in cold water overnight in fridge
Strain — the color is a deep, brilliant ruby red
Sweeten to taste — Egyptians like it sweet
Serve over ice with mint for the cold version
The deep red color is dramatic and beautiful
This is Egypt's national drink — served at every occasion, hot in winter, cold in summer
drinks.description: Egypt's ruby-red national drink — dried hibiscus flowers steeped into a tart, cranberry-like tea. Served blazing hot in winter or ice-cold in summer. The dramatic deep red pour and the health-benefit claims (it does lower blood pressure) have made karkade a viral wellness drink globally.
